description: Build a resident grid-wide n=512 QR megakernel that fuses FP32 Householder panels with tiled compact-WY updates without sacrificing GPU-wide parallelism: keep V/T in global slabs, schedule 128-column tcgen05/TMA update tasks through a device work queue, and use safe fully-resident phase barriers plus compensated TF32 arithmetic.

Resident 128-CTA grid with 32-matrix waves, FP32 NB32 panel owners, global V/T slabs, queued 128-column updates, and fully-resident epoch barriers; differential guard reached the n512 route but NVRTC rejected the added math.h include.

Removed unavailable math.h include; resident FP32 grid passed validation and all guards. Full geomean 1652.002351 us; dense batch640 n512 measured 93196.353 us. Nsys attributes 92.878 ms entirely to qr2_n512_resident_grid_fp32.

Replaced scalar WY updates with 16-warp WMMA TF32x3 tiles while retaining FP32 panels/T and the resident queue/barriers. NVRTC accepted the WMMA code but did not define __float_to_tf32 for explicit residual construction.

Used the WMMA namespace TF32 conversion helper; tensorized resident kernel compiled and ran, but dense n512 differential checks had factor residuals around 211-226 versus ~0.5 allowed, indicating an update layout/algebra error.

From the last known-good parent, tensorized only W=V^T C with compensated TF32x3 and kept C-=VZ scalar. Full validation passed. Geomean 1665.927285 us; dense batch640 n512 103381.686 us, versus 93196.353 us for the all-SIMT resident trial.

Tensorized C correction into a separate shared tile and subtracted explicitly, eliminating accumulator-load epilogue as a cause. Dense n512 still showed ~211-226 residual versus ~0.5 allowed, localizing the fault to the row-major VZ WMMA operand mapping.

Transposed the final WY product as (VZ)^T=Z^T V^T so both tensor products reuse the verified column-major compensated TF32x3 mapping. Full validation and guards passed. Geomean 1648.754638 us; dense batch640 n512 93068.105 us, essentially tied with the 93196.353 us all-SIMT resident trial and faster than tensor-W-only 103381.686 us.

Expanded resident wave from 32 to 128 matrices so every CTA owns a panel and global phase barriers occur one quarter as often; full validation and all guards passed, but the first full benchmark attempt was externally terminated with exit 143 before producing metrics.

Retried the validated WAVE=128 commit after the interrupted scheduler session. Full benchmark succeeded: geomean 1541.522264 us and dense batch640 n512 40973.335 us, a 2.27x speedup over WAVE=32 compensated tensorization at 93068.105 us, confirming panel concurrency and barrier-wave count dominated the resident design.

Kept the 128-matrix resident wave but replaced compensated WMMA updates with the original FP32 SIMT compact-WY column update, reducing block size to 256 and shared memory to ~71 KiB. Full validation passed. Geomean 1536.902675 us; dense n512 39659.942 us, 3.2% faster than compensated WMMA at 40973.335 us.

Doubled scalar compact-WY update tiles from 128 to 256 columns, matching all 256 threads and halving queued tasks plus redundant V/T shared loads. Full validation passed. Geomean 1509.351603 us; dense n512 31121.766 us, 21.5% faster than 128-column FP32 at 39659.942 us.

Expanded to one 512-column logical update task per matrix, with each 256-thread CTA processing up to two columns per thread. Full validation and guards passed, but the full benchmark process was terminated with exit 143 after about 98 seconds of active measurement and produced no metrics, consistent with a benchmark/infrastructure timeout or severe loop-spill slowdown.

Retried the already-validated 512-column logical tile after scheduler contention. Benchmark completed: geomean 1534.121542 us and dense n512 38795.360 us, 24.7% slower than 256-column tiles at 31121.766 us; serializing a second column per thread outweighs the saved slab load.

Restored the 256-column best and fused queue reset into the panel barrier, reducing per-panel global barriers from three to two. Full validation passed, but the first benchmark client was externally terminated with exit 143 before emitting metrics.

Retried the validated fused queue-reset barrier commit. Benchmark succeeded: geomean 1505.813402 us and dense n512 30808.344 us, 1.0% faster than the separate queue-reset barrier at 31121.766 us while preserving safe fully-resident epoch synchronization.

Expanded the fully resident grid from 128 to all 148 B200 SMs while retaining 128 panel owners. The shared build-scheduler client was externally terminated with exit 143 before NVRTC produced a result; source diff itself is clean.

Retry confirmed the 148-CTA grid compiles and passes full validation plus all guards. Its first benchmark attempt was externally terminated with exit 143 after acquiring the GPU but before metrics; retrying the unchanged validated commit.

Retried the validated 148-CTA fully resident grid. Benchmark succeeded: geomean 1503.355950 us and dense n512 30631.568 us, 0.57% faster than 128 CTAs at 30808.344 us. One CTA per B200 SM safely adds update capacity while 128 CTAs remain panel owners.

Best commit dc01a67c2989d2b92a594d39bf49820be44ea33b is fully validated and clean: resident NB32 Householder+compact-WY megakernel, global V/T slabs, device task queue, fused safe epoch barriers, WAVE=128, 256-column tasks, and 148 CTAs (one/B200 SM). Full geomean 1503.355950 us; dense batch640 n512 30631.568 us, 3.04x faster than the first resident FP32 trial (93196.353 us). Final nsys: resident kernel 30.381 ms / 99.9%, route probe 39.5 us. Compensated WMMA TF32x3 was made correct via transposed VZ but was slower than FP32 SIMT (40973 vs 39660 us at WAVE128); 512-column tasks regressed to 38795 us. Concrete openings: replace WMMA staging with direct sm100a tcgen05/TMEM plus TMA descriptors, instrument panel/update phase clocks, test NB16/NB64, and explore a two-CTA-per-matrix specialization that retains 256-column parallelism while reusing V/T. No leaderboard submission was made.

Build a resident grid-wide n=512 QR megakernel that fuses FP32 Householder panels with tiled compact-WY updates without sacrificing GPU-wide parallelism: keep V/T in global slabs, schedule 128-column tcgen05/TMA update tasks through a device work queue, and use safe fully-resident phase barriers plus compensated TF32 arithmetic.

Added low-overhead synchronized globaltimer instrumentation for release-to-release panel/update walls, per-CTA barrier wait, V/T staging, update math, and task counts; aggregate atomics occur only once per CTA at exit. Full validation passed. Dense n512 30942.630 us and geomean 1505.273505. One-shot counters: panel wall 16.688 ms, update wall 13.136 ms; 10,240 panel tasks averaged 203.46 us, 14,080 stage tasks 11.66 us and update math 98.43 us; aggregate barrier wait averaged 32.17 us across 24,420 CTA-barrier calls.

Reduced the resident panel width from NB32 to NB16 and resized V/T/shared slabs. Full validation passed. Geomean 1488.458763 us; dense n512 26466.053 us, 14.5% faster than instrumented NB32 at 30942.630 us. Phase walls moved from panel/update 16.688/13.136 ms to 9.858/15.598 ms; panel tasks halved to 58.15 us average while staging total stayed nearly flat (158.8 ms aggregate) and update math became the 61% wall bottleneck.

Expanded the resident panel width to NB64 and resized V/T/shared slabs. Full validation passed. Geomean 1565.205466 us; dense n512 48980.886 us. Phase counters show panel wall 34.816 ms and update wall 12.943 ms; 5,120 panel tasks averaged 864.04 us, versus NB16 panel wall 9.858 ms and 58.15 us/task. Update wall remained similar, so the regression is isolated to wide-panel factorization rather than staging.

Returned to NB16 and added static two-CTA Blackwell clusters. For two-tile phases, the root CTA stages each matrix V/T once and its partner consumes the slabs through distributed shared memory; one-tile phases retain independent CTA scheduling. Full validation passed. Dense n512 regressed to 41445.497 us, geomean 1545.596978. Staging fell from 158.8 to 93.9 ms aggregate (29,440 to 19,840 loads), but update math rose from 53.80 to 115.91 us/task because repeated remote-DSM operand reads dominate; panel remained 9.847 ms.

Refined paired clusters so the partner copies the root DSM V/T slabs once into local shared memory before update math. Full validation passed. Dense n512 recovered from 41445.497 to 26996.077 us; geomean 1491.893028. Update math returned to 53.32 us/task and staging aggregate fell 21.5% versus independent NB16 (124.6 vs 158.8 ms), but cluster synchronization/DSM replication raised update wall from 15.598 to 16.125 ms, leaving dense latency 2.0% above independent NB16.

Reduced paired-cluster wave size from 128 to 74 so every two-tile matrix maps to one of the 74 hardware clusters in a single round. Full validation passed. Dense n512 34415.624 us, geomean 1519.298547. Update wall improved from 16.125 to 15.260 ms and update tasks from 53.32 to 41.58 us, but nine lower-concurrency waves raised panel wall from 9.848 to 17.564 ms; measured panel concurrency dominates the saved cluster round.

Raised paired-cluster wave size from 74 to the full 148 resident CTAs and expanded V/T slabs, completing the low/high concurrency bracket. Full validation passed. Dense n512 26485.536 us, geomean 1488.089225. Phase walls were panel 9.888 ms and update 15.624 ms, recovering the WAVE128 panel concurrency and matching independent NB16 within noise while retaining clustered V/T sharing; WAVE74 measured 17.564/15.260 ms and 34415.624 us.

Reduced the clustered WAVE148 panel width from NB16 to NB8 to complete the lower-width crossover bracket. Full validation passed. Dense n512 regressed to 36324.541 us, geomean 1522.796970. Panel wall fell from 9.888 to 7.447 ms, but 64 panel/update phases raised update wall from 15.624 to 27.717 ms; NB16 is the measured crossover among NB8/16/32/64.

Produced a clean independent NB16/WAVE148 resident kernel after completing the instrumentation, width, and paired-cluster studies: removed globaltimer counters, timing allocation/atomics, static clusters, DSM replication, and cluster synchronizations while retaining 148 resident CTAs, 256-column queued updates, global V/T slabs, and fused epoch barriers. Full validation passed. Dense n512 25887.552 us; geomean 1482.724917, the lowest measured in brief 2.

Reduced the clean independent NB16 resident wave from 148 to 128 matrices while retaining all 148 CTAs, isolating panel-owner concurrency from instrumentation and clustered variants. Full validation and all guards passed. Dense n512 measured 26263.846 us and geomean 1487.137284 us, versus clean WAVE148 at 25887.552 us and 1482.724917 us; the 20 additional matrix slots improved dense latency by 1.43% despite the larger V/T workspace.

Continuation trials 18-27 measured the resident n512 phase balance and panel/update design space. Low-overhead globaltimer counters put NB32 at 16.688/13.136 ms panel/update. NB16 improved to 9.858/15.598 ms, NB64 shifted to 34.816/12.943 ms, and NB8 to 7.447/27.717 ms, making NB16 the measured width crossover. Two-CTA cluster sharing reduced aggregate V/T staging from 158.8 to 93.9 ms with direct DSM but remote inner-loop reads raised update math from 53.8 to 115.9 us/task; local shared replication restored 53.3 us/task but synchronization left dense at 26.996 ms. WAVE74 paired clusters measured 34.416 ms versus WAVE148 paired at 26.486 ms, confirming panel concurrency sensitivity. Removing counters and all cluster machinery produced the best measured commit 19c7f45819e0b6f36810d1aec3c19c02ec0d6f12: clean independent NB16/WAVE148, full-valid, dense 25887.552 us and geomean 1482.724917 us. A clean WAVE128 bracket at final commit abfc29cb31663ff3455fdfed188260825a3a6735 was full-valid but measured 26263.846 us and 1487.137284 us; its final nsys shows the resident kernel at 25.963 ms / 99.8% and route probe 39.1 us. Keep this objective moving: direct sm100a tcgen05/TMEM compact-WY updates remain open, as do TMA-based V/T staging, a pipelined cluster design that overlaps replication instead of synchronizing it, deeper NB16 panel reductions, and mixed-width late-panel specialization. No leaderboard submission was made.
